title: Backups
description: Every week, a full copy of your shop's records lands in storage you own. If you ever leave — or DiveDay ever disappears — the copy is already yours.

notice.saved: Backup destination saved. Run a test delivery to prove it works.
notice.invalid: Check the destination details and try again.
notice.endpoint_invalid: That endpoint doesn't read as a plain HTTPS address. Use your provider's bare S3 API origin, with no query, path, or credentials in it.
notice.endpoint_not_https: The endpoint must start with https:// — backups never travel unencrypted.
notice.endpoint_private_host: That endpoint points at a private or local address, which DiveDay's servers can't deliver to. Use your storage provider's public endpoint.
notice.secret_required: Enter the secret access key to connect this destination.
notice.encryption_key_unset: This DiveDay instance isn't set up to hold credentials safely yet, so nothing was saved.
notice.encryption_key_invalid: This DiveDay instance's encryption key is misconfigured, so nothing was saved.
notice.disconnected: Backup destination removed. The delivery history below stays.
notice.test_delivered: Test delivery landed in your bucket. Weekly backups are proven to work.
notice.no_destination: Save a destination first, then run a test delivery.
notice.not_authorized: Only an owner or manager can change backup settings.

status.notConfiguredDescription: Point DiveDay at an S3-compatible bucket you own — AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, and friends — and a full export bundle lands there every week.

form.heading: Destination
form.description: Any S3-compatible storage works. Use a credential that can only write to this bucket — DiveDay never needs to read, list, or delete anything in it.
form.endpointHint: Your provider's S3 API origin — HTTPS, with no bucket or path in it.
form.regionHint: The signing region — “auto” on Cloudflare R2, “us-east-1” style on AWS.
form.prefixHint: Bundles land inside this folder in the bucket.
form.secretHint: Stored sealed, used only to sign uploads, and never shown again — not even to you.
form.secretKeepHint: Leave blank to keep the current key; enter a new one only to rotate it.

how.heading: How it works
how.weekly: Once a week, DiveDay builds your full export bundle — every CSV, the README, your photos — and delivers it to your bucket. It's the same bundle as the Data export download, so what you'd take when leaving is what gets backed up.
how.contents: Your trip schedule rides along as trips.ics, readable by any calendar app.
how.sealed: The secret access key is sealed before it's stored and opened only at the moment of upload.
how.failures: A delivery that fails is recorded below and tried again on the next weekly run — DiveDay never hammers your bucket with retries.

history.heading: Delivery history
history.empty: No deliveries yet. Once a destination is saved, every weekly and test delivery shows up here.

deliveryError.upload_unauthorized: The bucket refused the credential — check the access key and its write permission.
deliveryError.bucket_not_found: No bucket by that name answered at the endpoint — check both.
deliveryError.upload_rejected: The storage provider rejected the upload.
deliveryError.credential_unreadable: The stored secret key can't be opened any more — enter it again to fix this.
deliveryError.shop_missing: The shop's records couldn't be loaded.
deliveryError.bundle_failed: The export bundle couldn't be built.
deliveryError.encryption_key_unset: This DiveDay instance isn't set up to hold credentials safely.
deliveryError.encryption_key_invalid: This DiveDay instance's encryption key is misconfigured.

disconnect.heading: Remove destination
disconnect.description: Deletes the stored credential and stops weekly deliveries. The history below and everything already in your bucket stay put.
